participation.context: Came in before the gate with wet shoes, and brought three boughs down to one.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

participation.context: Allowed one bough, refused a ribbon, and refused a wood.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Accepted the one, and went up with the old man in his head.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Stayed on the book and was not moved.
participation.name: Gib

relations.note: one bough is the whole custom
relations.quote: One bough over the door, and no more.

story.body: You stood by her allowance and did not ask for a second or a ribbon. You ate a mouthful, left the cat, and went to the gate. You did not tell the house where Sunday's dinner is.

relations.note: one bough is the whole custom
relations.quote: One bough over the door, and no more.

title: Stood by one bough and went up to the gate

participation.context: attendee in Hawthorn on the arch
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: You looked at the hawthorn and the ribbons on the gate, and you did not take any of it home.

participation.context: attendee in A garland over the mud
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: You saw the garland go over the dirt, held high. The picture is the one you kept.

title: Saw the garland carried above the mud
